content:
Diego Santos: Hey folks — quick alignment needed on metric naming + label conventions for the new Private backup/restore jobs. We’re about to wire this into control plane + the CronJobs (and observability-pack dashboards/alerts). What’s the canonical prefix + required labels? Want to avoid us inventing 3 different schemas.

Sergio Costa: +1. I’m updating the dashboard panels and I’m seeing three variants in the PRs/branches:
- `redwood_backup_*`
- `rw_private_backup_*`
- `redwood_private_dr_*`

Allison Grant: We should follow Prometheus best practices + Redwood internal conventions:
- prefix: `redwood_private_backup_...` for backup-specific metrics, `redwood_private_restore_...` for restore-specific
- counters end with `_total`
- durations as histograms with `_seconds`
- gauges for “last successful backup timestamp/age”

Allison Grant: Strong request: keep label cardinality tight. Absolutely no `backup_id`, no object key/path, no per-file metrics.

Diego Santos: Makes sense. In installer PR 842 we used `rw-private-dr` as the CLI name — but metric prefix doesn’t have to mirror that.

Sergio Costa: Can we standardize on a small required label set? The dashboards need to group by cluster + backup “scope” at least.

Allison Grant: Proposed required labels (backup metrics):
- `private_cluster` (string, stable human name; not uid)
- `namespace` (k8s namespace)
- `mode` = `scheduled|manual`
- `scope` = `control_plane_db|object_store|config_policy|secrets_certs` (or whatever final inventory says)
- `backend` = `s3|minio|nfs|gcs|azureblob|filesystem` (even if not all ship in v1)
- `outcome` = `success|failure|skipped`

Allison Grant: Optional labels:
- `reason` only on failures/skips and only from a bounded enum list (permissions, timeout, lock_contention, config_invalid, checksum_mismatch, encryption_error, unknown)
- `encryption` = `kms|hsm|local|none` (note: if we ever have “none” it should be explicit)

Sergio Costa: Love it. For “last successful backup age” I usually do:
- `redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{...}` gauge
Then a dashboard expression for “age” = `time() - last_success_timestamp_seconds`.

Allison Grant: Yep. Avoid pushing “age” as a gauge from the job itself (clocks + scrape timing get weird). Timestamp is good.

Diego Santos: For duration: do we want histogram on total job wall clock + separate per-phase durations (pg_dump vs upload)?

Allison Grant: Minimum:
- `redwood_private_backup_duration_seconds` histogram (end-to-end)
Nice-to-have (only if phase count is fixed and low):
- `redwood_private_backup_phase_duration_seconds{phase="quiesce|db_dump|wal_archive|artifact_snapshot|upload|verify"}` histogram
But if phase label gets abused, it’s a cardinality trap.

Ethan Park: Jumping in — control plane can emit events around maintenance/quiesce boundaries (PR 18421). If we want phase metrics, better to standardize phases in code, not free-form strings from the CLI.

Sergio Costa: Also for alerts: I need a counter to compute success rate + a gauge for “last success”. So:
- `redwood_private_backup_runs_total{outcome=...}` counter
- `redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds` gauge
- `redwood_private_backup_last_attempt_timestamp_seconds` gauge (maybe)

Allison Grant: Agree. “runs_total” is the anchor metric.
Naming suggestion:
- `redwood_private_backup_run_total` vs `..._runs_total`?
Prometheus style is plural-ish but not strict. I lean `..._runs_total`.

Sean Gallagher: From SRE side: keep it consistent with SLO toolkit. We’ll likely do an objective like “backup success rate per cluster over 28d”. Having `..._runs_total{outcome}` makes that easy.

Miles Thornton: +1 on SRE needs. Also, for DR drills we’ll want annotation-friendly metrics around restores, but for backups the big questions are:
- did it run?
- did it succeed?
- how long?
- how stale is the last success?

Diego Santos: For label names: do we want `cluster` vs `private_cluster`? I worry “cluster” collides with other Redwood hosted metrics.

Allison Grant: Use `private_cluster`. We already have `cluster` in some runtime metrics and it’s ambiguous. Also do NOT label by customer name.

Sergio Costa: What about region / environment? Some Private installs are multi-region.

Allison Grant: Optional label `site` = `primary|secondary` or `region` if it’s well-defined. But don’t invent it in the jobs unless installer provides it. Prefer `region` only if it’s a low-cardinality known value (e.g. `us-east-1`).

Diego Santos: OK. Another question: should we label the schedule name? (some customers run multiple backup CronJobs for different scopes)

Allison Grant: Avoid `cronjob` label unless absolutely necessary. It explodes cardinality across namespaces. If we need it, make it `schedule` with bounded values we control (e.g. `hourly|daily|weekly`).

Sergio Costa: That works. For multiple scopes, you can separate with `scope` anyway.

Ethan Park: For the “skipped” outcome — when would we skip?

Diego Santos: If cluster is in “paused” mode or backups are disabled by policy; also if we detect an overlapping run (concurrency guard).

Allison Grant: Great — treat those as `outcome="skipped"` with `reason="paused"|"overlap"|"disabled"`.

Sergio Costa: Draft metric list (backup):
- `redwood_private_backup_runs_total{private_cluster,namespace,mode,scope,backend,outcome,reason?}`
- `redwood_private_backup_duration_seconds_bucket{...}` + sum/count
- `redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{private_cluster,namespace,mode,scope,backend}`
- `redwood_private_backup_bytes_total{...}` counter? (size uploaded)

Allison Grant: Size is useful. Use:
- `redwood_private_backup_bytes_total` counter (bytes written to backend)
No “current bytes” gauge.

Sean Gallagher: Please keep `reason` out of the high-volume duration histograms if possible. Otherwise you’ll get tons of series.

Allison Grant: +1. Best practice:
- Put `reason` only on the runs counter (and only on failure/skip samples).
- Histograms: only stable dimensions (`private_cluster, namespace, mode, scope, backend, outcome`). Even `outcome` on histogram is debatable; but it’s usually fine if it’s just success/failure.

Diego Santos: If outcome on histogram is too much, we can just record durations on success only.

Allison Grant: That’s acceptable. If we do that, document it clearly so people don’t misread “duration” as including failures.

Sergio Costa: For dashboards I’m fine with “duration of successful backups” as long as we have a separate panel for failure rate.

Diego Santos: Cool. I’ll update the instrumentation in the job runner to:
- emit `runs_total` always
- emit `duration_seconds` only on success
- emit `last_success_timestamp_seconds` on success
- emit `bytes_total` on success

Allison Grant: Perfect. Please also add `redwood_private_backup_build_info{version, git_sha}` gauge (value=1) to help support correlate behavior with installer/CLI version.

Diego Santos: Nice call.

Sergio Costa: Can we write this down somewhere? I’ll mirror it into the observability-pack PR description and link it from the Confluence observability spec.

Allison Grant: Yep — drop a short “metrics contract” section into the Confluence page and we’ll treat it as the source of truth. Also, when you add metrics, include a sample scrape block in the PR so reviewers can sanity check.

Diego Santos: Will do. I’ll post a follow-up snippet once I push.

Sergio Costa: :thumbsup: (also, please keep label keys snake_case; no camelCase)

Allison Grant: +1 snake_case.

Diego Santos: Noted. Thanks all.
